what_its_for: Linezolid is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including skin infections, pneumonia (lung infection), and infections caused by bacteria that are resistant to other antibiotics, such as MRSA (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus) and VRE (vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus).
how_to_take: Take linezolid exactly as your doctor prescribes. You can take it with or without food. If you are taking the liquid (oral suspension), gently mix it by turning the bottle upside down 3 to 5 times before each use — do NOT shake it vigorously. Use the measuring device provided to get the right dose. Finish all of your medication even if you start feeling better. Stopping early can allow the infection to come back or become harder to treat.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 400 mg to 600 mg taken every 12 hours (twice a day) for 10 to 28 days, depending on the type of infection. Your doctor will decide the right dose and length of treatment for you. For children, the dose is based on weight and age. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store linezolid tablets and oral suspension at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the oral suspension bottle tightly closed and use it within 21 days of opening. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating large amounts of foods high in tyramine while taking linezolid, as this can cause a dangerous rise in blood pressure. Foods to limit or avoid include aged cheeses, cured or processed meats (like salami and pepperoni), fermented foods, soy sauce, tap beer, red wine, and overripe or dried fruits. Avoid taking linezolid with certain medications, including MAO inhibitors (like phenelzine or selegiline), certain antidepressants (such as SSRIs like fluoxetine or sertraline), or decongestants (like pseudoephedrine), as dangerous interactions can occur. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking. Avoid alcohol during treatment.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe headache, stiff neck, fast or irregular heartbeat, sudden high blood pressure, confusion, or agitation (these may be signs of a dangerous drug interaction called serotonin syndrome or hypertensive crisis); vision changes or blurred vision; numbness, tingling, or weakness in your hands or feet; seizures; severe diarrhea that is watery or bloody; unusual bruising or bleeding; pale skin, extreme tiredness, or shortness of breath (possible signs of low blood cell counts); or signs of a severe allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting linezolid, but it is very important to finish the entire course of treatment prescribed by your doctor. If your symptoms do not improve after a few days or get worse, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of linezolid during pregnancy has not been well established, and it may pass into breast milk. Your doctor will weigh the benefits and risks for you. Children: Linezolid can be used in children, but the dose will be adjusted based on the child's weight and age. Older adults: No specific dose adjustment is usually needed for older adults, but they may be more sensitive to side effects and should be monitored closely. Kidney or liver disease: Linezolid does not generally require dose changes for kidney or liver problems, but tell your doctor about any kidney or liver conditions you have.
